record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: For quotient rings R = S/I where I is a monomial ideal or projective toric ideal, find classes of I for which Macaulay-type behavior holds over R: every Hilbert function over R is attained by a lex ideal in R.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be a polynomial ring over a field $k$, graded by total degree, and let $I \subset S$ be a homogeneous ideal. The quotient $R = S/I$ inherits a standard grading. A monomial ideal $L \subset S$ containing $I$ is called a lex ideal in $R$ if, for every monomial $m \in L$ and every monomial $m'$ of the same degree with $m' \geq_{\mathrm{lex}} m$ (in the lexicographic order on monomials of $S$), one has $m' \in L$. The Hilbert function of a graded $R$-module $M$ is $H_M(d) = \dim_k M_d$.

The ring $R$ is said to be Macaulay-Lex if for every homogeneous ideal $J \subset R$ there exists a lex ideal $L \subset R$ with $H_{R/J} = H_{R/L}$; equivalently, every Hilbert function of a graded quotient of $R$ is attained by a lex ideal in $R$.

Problem. Identify and characterize broad classes of ideals $I \subset S$ for which $R = S/I$ is Macaulay-Lex, in each of the following settings:
(a) $I$ is a monomial ideal of $S$;
(b) $I$ is the homogeneous ideal defining a projective toric variety (i.e., the kernel of a homomorphism $S \to k[t_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, t_m^{\pm 1}]$ sending each $x_i$ to a Laurent monomial, all of the same degree under some grading).

Find general structural conditions on $I$ (combinatorial in case (a), or in terms of the associated lattice/semigroup data in case (b)) that are sufficient, and ideally necessary, for $R$ to be Macaulay-Lex.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open in general. Known Macaulay-Lex classes include the Clements–Lindström rings (quotients by powers of variables), squarefree analogues, and certain colored quotient rings (Mermin–Murai and others, ca. 2008–2014). For projective toric rings, Gasharov–Horwitz–Peeva (2008) gave partial sufficient conditions, but no general classification of monomial or toric ideals giving Macaulay-Lex quotients is known.

status_evidence.title: Hilbert Functions over Toric Rings (Gasharov–Horwitz–Peeva)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes sufficient conditions for every Hilbert function of a monomial ideal in a projective toric ring to be attained by a lex ideal.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for toric rings; full classification not known.

status_evidence.title: Hilbert functions of colored quotient rings and a generalization of the Clements–Lindström theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies new families (colored quotient rings) that are Macaulay-Lex, generalizing the Clements–Lindström theorem.
status_evidence.claim: New Macaulay-Lex classes continue to be discovered, indicating the general classification problem is open.

status_evidence.title: Betti numbers of lex ideals over some Macaulay-Lex rings
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Macaulay-Lex rings as an active class without a complete characterization.
status_evidence.claim: The class of Macaulay-Lex quotient rings is studied piecemeal, supporting open status.
